content.title: About
content.content: Beef hot dog is a sausage made from ground beef, seasoned with spices and placed in a soft bun. It is a popular fast‑food item often served with mustard, ketchup, pickles, and onions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The beef hot dog appeared in the United States in the early 20th century as a cheaper alternative to the traditional pork version.
In some U.S. regions (e.g., Chicago) a distinct style is served without ketchup but with mustard, pickles, and tomato relish.
The bun is usually baked with milk and butter, giving it a soft, slightly sweet texture.
Beef sausage typically contains about 15‑20 % fat, which keeps the product juicy.
In several countries the hot dog is considered a national snack, such as Japan where it is often topped with teriyaki sauce.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: A beef hot dog provides roughly 12 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Beef provides zinc, which supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and modest fat helps promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef hot dogs contain saturated fats that, when eaten frequently, may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some versions include nitrites and other preservatives that are considered undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may be allergic to beef or to the spices used in the sausage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the hot dog in a split bun, adding mustard, ketchup, mayo, pickles, onions, or cheese to taste. It can be cooked on a grill, skillet, or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen versions last up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before eating.
